1.explanation:
1. RadioButton.js
   • This component renders the <label> with aria-label instead of relying on its child text or associating the accessible name with the <input>. Because screen readers focus on the input’s accessible name, putting aria-label on the label element prevents the actual text from being announced. The fix is to move or remove aria-label on the <label> and let the nested <span> with labelText supply the accessible name (or apply aria-label / aria-labelledby directly to the <input>).

2. RadioButtonGroup.js
   • The group wrapper is just a <div> and plain text, so there’s no fieldset/legend or aria grouping. Screen readers don’t link the group heading to its radio buttons. Replacing the wrapper with a <fieldset> and rendering the heading as a <legend> (or adding appropriate aria-role and aria-labelledby) will ensure the group label is announced together with each radio button.
1.bug_scenario: When navigating the React radio-button examples with VoiceOver (or JAWS), the screen reader fails to announce the human-readable label text. In the vanilla HTML version the label text “Radio button label” is read correctly, but in the React version VoiceOver only reports “selected, radio button, 1 of X” (or even just “selected, radio button”), omitting the actual label. A second screenshot of a grouped example shows that the group heading (“Radio Button heading”) also isn’t announced as part of the accessible name. Both issues stem from how the React components generate label and group markup for assistive technologies.
